replies.author: @tysoncung
replies.text: No new RBMK has been built since, but the design was never retired: Kursk, Smolensk and Leningrad still run RBMK units today. After 1986 the surviving reactors were modified, including more fixed absorbers in the core, enrichment raised so the void coefficient fell, and the control rods changed so the graphite tips could not displace water at the bottom of the core, which is the step that turned the shutdown into a power surge.
